details.summary: A flavorful and well-designed plant-based Mediterranean skillet that perfectly fits the book's nutritional and everyday-cooking goals. However, it requires a necessary fix to add the missing steeping time for the couscous in the instructions.

dimensions.feedback: The savory, tangy Mediterranean flavors (lemon, sun-dried tomatoes, feta, oregano) are robust enough to beautifully balance the earthy flavor of the tempeh.
Every listed ingredient is used properly in the instructions, and no surprise ingredients are introduced.

Step 6 instructs the reader to let the couscous stand off the heat to steep, but provides no time duration. Fix: Add 'for 5 minutes' to Step 6 so the cook knows when the grains are tender. (Also, update the metadata Cook Time from 7 minutes to 12 minutes to account for this steep).
While tempeh is traditionally Indonesian, it functions perfectly here as a high-protein, plant-based vehicle for classic Mediterranean flavors.
Using the residual heat and cooking liquid to steep the couscous directly in the skillet is a smart, effective one-pan technique.

The computed values align precisely with the ingredients. The slight overages in saturated fat (5.9g vs 5g ceiling) and carbohydrate (55.6g vs 55g ceiling) are accurate consequences of the feta and couscous, and do not represent a data flaw.
The title is descriptive, and the intro provides a warm, practical, and accurate overview of the nutritional benefits without resorting to banned 'diet' or 'detox' language.
An excellent, quick weeknight dinner. The one-pan format is highly appealing and cleanup is minimal.
Delivers perfectly on the dual-focus of the book: high-quality complex carbohydrates (whole-wheat couscous), abundant fiber, solid vegetable presence, and a clean plant-based protein.
There is zero added sugar, and the carbohydrate component is an excellent, intact whole-grain source that fits neatly into the main dinner target window.

An ideal meatless dinner delivering 34.7g of protein, well over the 26g floor, proving that plant-based meals can easily hit the required protein tier. (The minor saturated fat overage from the feta is acceptable here).
Even with the 5-minute couscous steep accounted for, this easily clocks in at 22 minutes total from a cold start. All ingredients are readily available at standard supermarkets.

details.summary: This is a flavorful, well-conceived plant-based skillet that uses tempeh cleverly in a Mediterranean context. However, it requires a structural fix to the couscous-to-broth ratio to prevent it from becoming soggy, and slight reductions to the feta and sun-dried tomatoes to meet the book's strict carbohydrate, saturated fat, and calorie ceilings.

dimensions.feedback: The flavors are well-balanced. Mediterranean ingredients like artichokes, sun-dried tomatoes, feta, and oregano pair nicely with the nutty, savory depth of the tempeh.
All listed ingredients are used properly in the instructions, and no surprise ingredients are introduced.

Step 2 provides a time range ('4 to 5 minutes') but lacks a specific prompt to check at the minimum time. Update to: 'Cook, stirring occasionally, and check at 4 minutes. Continue cooking up to 5 minutes until golden brown...'
While tempeh is Indonesian, the intro successfully frames it as an 'unexpected anchor' for a Mediterranean flavor profile. The fusion works beautifully for a plant-based chapter.

The ratio of dry couscous (1/2 cup) to broth (1 cup) is too high. Standard couscous uses a 1:1 ratio by volume. Even with the sun-dried tomatoes absorbing some moisture, 1 cup of broth will result in a soupy or mushy texture after a 5-minute rest. Reduce the broth to 1/2 or 2/3 cup.
The computed nutrition panel aligns logically with the specified ingredients, given the carbohydrate density of dry couscous and sun-dried tomatoes, and the saturated fat from feta.
The title names the hero ingredients accurately, and the intro is warmly written without any banned 'detox' or exaggerated health claims.
A fast, hearty, one-skillet dinner with high protein and excellent fiber. The textures of the crumbled tempeh, tender artichokes, and fluffy couscous are highly appealing.
Strongly aligned. It utilizes a high-quality whole grain (whole-wheat couscous), a lean plant protein (tempeh), plenty of vegetables, and heart-healthy olive oil.
Zero added sugar, and the dish centers on a legitimate, complex whole-grain carbohydrate that stabilizes blood sugar.

The recipe exceeds the dinner nutrient ceilings for saturated fat (6.8g vs 5g limit), carbohydrates (62.3g vs 55g limit), and energy (590 kcal vs 540 limit). To pull it into range, reduce the feta cheese to 2 tablespoons (saving ~3g sat fat) and the sun-dried tomatoes to 1/4 cup (saving ~7.5g carbs and ~35 kcal).
Easily achieved in 30 minutes from a cold start. Minimal chopping and a very rapid skillet-to-steam cooking technique make it exceptionally practical.
